issues.title: Persistent USE KEYSPACE failure drains pool and marks node permanently Down
issues.verdictReason: handle_ready_connection's new Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace) arm (connection_pool.rs:900-910) discards the connection and, once the pool is empty, calls update_shared_conns which sets MaybePoolConnections::Broken, which emit_events turns into ConnectivityChangeEvent::Lost (node Down). On main, a failed USE only warned and the connection was kept in the pool. The PR description confirms this is the intended fail-closed behavior, but it does mean a node whose keyspace can never be set now goes fully and durably unreachable instead of degrading.
issues.scopeReason: This is exactly the new discard-on-keyspace-failure behavior the PR adds.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Permanently failing USE keyspace leaves the connection pool unable to ever refill

reportedAsByRun.rafp-coverage-2026-10-04/quillstone/revi: If the keyspace can never be USEd, every connection opened afterward fails USE and is discarded, so pools drain to Broken(UseKeyspaceError), nodes go Down, and the node becomes permanently unusable; on base these connections were kept with a warning.

issues.title: Refill loop keeps reopening and discarding connections while USE keeps failing
issues.verdictReason: Each Keyspace-error connection sets had_error_since_last_refill and need_filling() stays true, so the existing refill/backoff loop in run() (connection_pool.rs:719-726) keeps scheduling start_filling(), which reopens TCP+STARTUP+USE only to discard it again; this churn mechanism is pre-existing (it already applies to plain connection failures) but is now also triggered by unrecoverable keyspace errors.
issues.scopeReason: The new Keyspace-error path makes this pre-existing churn mechanism reachable for a failure mode it didn't previously apply to.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Repeated reconnect churn when USE keeps failing

reportedAsByRun.rafp-coverage-2026-10-04/quillstone/revi: With a USE that always fails and some connections still alive, every refill tick (at most every 10s) reopens the whole connection shortfall (TCP, STARTUP, auth), and each connection is then thrown away.

issues.title: Stale failed USE attempt isn't re-checked against the current keyspace before being…
issues.verdictReason: The Ok arm explicitly re-checks evt.keyspace_name against self.current_keyspace and retries with the new keyspace if it changed (connection_pool.rs:913-925), but the Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace(err)) arm has no equivalent check and unconditionally drops the connection; a USE that fails only because the keyspace changed mid-flight is treated the same as a genuinely-broken keyspace.
issues.scopeReason: The asymmetry exists only because this PR added the Keyspace-error branch.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Stale USE result is treated as a failure instead of being compared against the current…

reportedAsByRun.rafp-coverage-2026-10-04/quillstone/revi: The Keyspace error arm never compares evt.keyspace_name with current_keyspace; if the keyspace changed while USE was in flight and the old USE fails, the connection is dropped and counted as a fill error, whereas the Ok arm would have retried it with the new keyspace.

issues.title: Keyspace-setup failure now logs at debug! instead of the prior warn!
issues.verdictReason: connection_pool.rs:904 logs the new Keyspace-error path at debug!, whereas the old start_setting_keyspace_for_connection future used warn! for the same failure; this does reduce default-level visibility for a failure that can now empty the pool. It is however consistent with the sibling Connection-error arm in the same function, which already logs non-shard-aware connection failures at debug! even when they empty the pool, so it isn't an isolated downgrade, just an extension of that existing convention to the new error type.
issues.scopeReason: The log level change happens in code this PR rewrote.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Log level dropped from warn! to debug! for a failure that can disable the pool

reportedAsByRun.rafp-coverage-2026-10-04/quillstone/revi: This failure now drops connections and can disable the pool, yet nothing shows at default log levels, while the related 'Failed to change keyspace' message still uses warn!.

issues.title: Commit 0d91aa54 fails clippy on its own under default features
issues.verdictReason: Checked out commit 0d91aa54 in a worktree and ran `cargo clippy -p scylla --lib --all-targets -- -D warnings`: it fails with `error: unused import: futures::FutureExt` at connection_pool.rs:1445, because that commit's only use of FutureExt-provided methods in the test module is inside a #[cfg(feature = "metrics")]-gated test. The final squashed tree (HEAD) is clean since a later commit uses it unconditionally too, but this intermediate commit breaks the CONTRIBUTING.md requirement that every commit in the patch passes static checks.
issues.scopeReason: The commit is authored by this PR.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-coverage-2026-10-04/quillstone/revi: The commit adds use futures::FutureExt; without a feature gate, but the import is only used inside a #[cfg(feature = "metrics")] test, so under default features make clippy (-Dwarnings --all-targets) fails at that commit, breaking the CONTRIBUTING rule that every commit passes static checks.

issues.title: No test drives the full failed-USE-then-refill cycle via the real event loop
issues.verdictReason: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill only calls handle_ready_connection once with a synthetic error and asserts need_filling() is true; keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state sets refiller.current_keyspace directly rather than going through the public use_keyspace request path, and never actually runs refiller.run() to observe a subsequent connection attempt after a keyspace failure. The permanently-broken-pool consequence described in I1 is therefore asserted only indirectly (via need_filling()/is_empty()), not exercised end-to-end.
issues.scopeReason: These are the new tests this PR adds for the new failure path.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: No test exercises the main failure path of a failed use_keyspace followed by a refill

reportedAsByRun.rafp-coverage-2026-10-04/quillstone/revi: No test drives a failed use_keyspace followed by a refill; the new tests set refiller.current_keyspace directly, so the permanently-unusable-node finding is untested.

issues.title: Reshard metrics test can't detect a dropped excess_connections term in the decrement
issues.verdictReason: Traced resharding_discards_old_connections_and_balances_metrics: at the point maybe_reshard runs, excess_connections is always empty in this test (only one connection exists per shard throughout), so self.decrement_total_connections(self.active_connection_count() + self.excess_connections.len()) at connection_pool.rs:1118-1120 would behave identically if the `+ self.excess_connections.len()` term were deleted. The test cannot catch a regression that stops decrementing metrics for discarded excess connections during a reshard.
issues.scopeReason: This is a gap in a test this PR added.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Reshard metrics test cannot catch a missing term in the decrement

reportedAsByRun.rafp-coverage-2026-10-04/quillstone/revi: The test reshards with zero excess connections, so it would still pass even if excess_connections.len() were removed from the decrement.

issues.title: The !is_filling() guard on keyspace-failure pool reporting is untested
issues.verdictReason: In keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill, ready_connections is empty before and during the call, so is_filling() is already false regardless of the guard; no test has a keyspace failure arrive while other connections are still being opened (is_filling() true) and the pool is empty, so removing the `!self.is_filling() &&` guard at connection_pool.rs:908 would not be caught by any current test.
issues.scopeReason: Gap in the new test coverage this PR adds for the new branch.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-coverage-2026-10-04/quillstone/revi: No test has a keyspace failure while other connections are still being set up and the pool is empty, so removing the guard would go unnoticed.

issues.title: Decrement-then-clear pattern is duplicated at each call site rather than centralized
issues.verdictReason: self.decrement_total_connections(...) immediately followed by .clear() is repeated verbatim at connection_pool.rs:674-676 and :1031-1032, and a similar decrement-then-conns.clear() pairing appears in maybe_reshard (:1118-1120); decrement_total_connections only wraps the counter loop, not the 'drop connections and keep the metric balanced' invariant itself, so a future edit could add a new clearing site and forget the matching decrement.
issues.scopeReason: All three call sites were added or touched by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Metric decrements are hand-copied at each call site instead of centralized

reportedAsByRun.rafp-coverage-2026-10-04/quillstone/revi: The decrement-then-clear pair is repeated at multiple sites with no helper owning 'drop connections and keep the metric balanced,' so future edits can let the metric drift again.
